claims.text: High configurational entropy favors formation of a coherent, nanostructured multiphase microstructure in lightweight HEAs.
The coherent nanostructured multiphase microstructure stabilizes finely dispersed intermetallic-strengthening precipitates.
The proposed microstructure promotes an adherent protective oxide film during high-temperature exposure.
High configurational entropy stabilizes a metastable nanostructured state.
Finely dispersed precipitates mechanically reinforce the alloy matrix.
Certain alloying elements segregate to the surface to form a continuous protective oxide film.
The continuous oxide film provides corrosion resistance.
The continuous oxide film provides high-temperature oxidation resistance.
Under controlled thermal aging, the HEA will maintain or improve its mechanical strength relative to a similar-density, lower-entropy baseline alloy.
Under controlled thermal aging, the HEA will maintain or improve its corrosion resistance relative to the baseline alloy.
Under controlled thermal aging, the HEA will maintain or improve its oxidation resistance relative to the baseline alloy.
Aged HEA samples should contain coherent, uniformly dispersed nanoprecipitates.
Aged HEA samples should develop an adherent protective oxide layer.
Lower configurational entropy limits the baseline alloy's capacity to form the proposed stabilized nanostructure.
Very high temperatures or prolonged exposure can drive extensive phase separation and precipitate coarsening.
Extensive phase separation and precipitate coarsening cause the predicted synergistic benefits to cease.
Aggressive oxidizing conditions can destroy the protective oxide film and eliminate the predicted benefits.

contradictions.description: The prediction permits the HEA merely to maintain performance relative to the baseline, whereas the falsification rule requires it to be consistently superior across tested conditions. An equal-performance result could therefore satisfy the stated prediction while also triggering falsification.
